route: The worklight tower is a released place and render package. The world instantiates a Helios Half-Shift cluster instance and two Vesta faction-berth instances when their sites are admitted; counterweightCircuit creates two fixtures in Pallas Drift. POI landmark data, Breakwater Spur and the UI stage also reference it. Everyday station-kit dressing can select it without replacement, at most once per sector. Placement and visibility remain conditional on residency, site and camera.
status: Source placement, material/LOD data and renderer ownership traced; a Breakwater frame-origin correction passed focused tests and LOD0 was visually inspected in current isolated multi-angle captures. LOD1/2, player-route pictures and performance remain unverified.
notes: The Ceres occupational-yard worklight data has no caller in src and is not evidence of a spawned yard placement.
Place boundaries start on lod0 and can resolve different LODs by projected size; no runtime tier frequency has been sampled.
Forge merges the floodhead geometry by material and LOD; eligible place surfaces are further statically batched per boundary. Cross-boundary instancing must be observed rather than assumed.

Ordinary fx dressing has no Nocturne override and does not automatically receive Nocturne's archetype fixtures; the authored crown uses emissive materials. The UI stage has its own explicit practical lights.

The Breakwater Spur owner independently creates up to four physical PointLights, including one at the worklight head. Its group now follows the frame origin; the focused scene-graph check covers initial nonzero origin, rebase and missing origin. Ordinary route and visual acceptance remain unverified.

Three-Lamp Corner currently uses the ordinary eight-head worklight model, not a separate playable material/geometry variant. The isolated world owner probe shows a FULL-residency fx actor and REDUCED-residency dressing row with no collision, lamp stage or NOCTURNE fixture descriptor. Its related Pigeon Day sequence emits transient VFX cues rather than modifying individual model lamps.
